method: Live execution (not just test-suite reference) of the actual reader code this session, against a 123-row Dv34-shaped and 50-row Watchtower-shaped fixture, each split across HOT/COLD, measuring both correctness AND latency.
dv34_full_classification_preserved_note: This test proves the RAW ROW COUNT (123) survives tiering. The evidence-QUALIFICATION breakdown (23 HIGH / 82 valid-not-HIGH / 18 historical-only, per docs/audits/of_dv34_p3_main_db_70_vs_new_23_reconciliation.json) is a property of a SEPARATE classification layer (the discovery corpus's direct_funding_edges table), not of transfer_index itself -- that classification is computed by joining against transfer_index by signature, which is identical in HOT and COLD schemas, so the classification remains computable identically regardless of tier. Not re-run end-to-end this pass (would require the full OF-DV34-P3 pipeline against a synthetic fixture, out of scope for this storage-focused milestone) -- the row-count-preservation proof is the storage-layer-relevant guarantee, and it holds.
3sw2_note: 3SW2's real structure (1 canonical entity per docs/audits/ops_ui_p1_unified_operations_read_model.json) is a strict subset-shape of this Watchtower control (fewer entities, same query mechanics) -- not independently re-run with distinct fixture data this pass; same limitation disclosed in P3, carried forward honestly rather than silently claimed as tested.
conclusion: Both hard reference controls confirm ZERO row loss and sub-millisecond query latency across a HOT/COLD split using the actual production-capable UnifiedTransferReader code (not a simplified stand-in).
